title: The Ledger of Bellwether Lane
premise: Five years ago, the drowning death of teenager Wren Halloway was ruled an accident, and retired detective Noor Crane quietly buried the doubts that ended their career. When a letter arrives confessing to Wren's murder — postmarked the day after the funeral of the man everyone blamed — Noor reopens the case from behind the counter of their failing bookshop, following a trail of forged ledgers, borrowed identities, and a tide chart that doesn't lie. The killer turns out to be the town's beloved harbormaster, who has been living under a dead man's name for thirty years and killed Wren to keep it buried. In the end, Noor must choose between handing the evidence to a police force that once discarded them or letting the tide keep Bellwether Lane's oldest secret — and they choose justice, at the cost of the only community they have left.
about_author: Odile Dunmore is the pen name of a former coastal records clerk who spent a decade filing other people's disappearances. They write mysteries about small towns that keep their secrets alphabetized.
